before.name: Logix Aurelia 16 KB RAM expansion card
before.description: Optional 16 KB RAM card occupying one Plug and Execute expansion slot. On Aurelia it increases installed RAM from 48 KB to 64 KB. The mapper exposes its four 4 KB pages at B000–EFFF in the normal application view; ROM and video RAM can temporarily overlay those pages without erasing their contents.

memory_mapping.configuration: Firmware discovers the card at startup and maps its pages; no manual address switches.
memory_mapping.system_workspace: The existing 4 KB common system RAM remains at F000–FFFF; the card adds 16 KB to lower RAM.
memory_mapping.service_calls: The common-memory runtime saves the RAM mapping, selects ROM/video RAM for a service and restores the card pages before returning.
memory_mapping.installation: Install with power off, then restart so firmware can discover and test the card.
memory_mapping.application_memory: Lower RAM rises from 44 KB to 60 KB, before other system and workspace reservations.

physical_population.refresh_owner: Host memory controller must refresh the card even while its pages are overlaid; exact interface pending.

Buffer policy: Local adapter RAM, additional to host system RAM. Partition transmit/receive buffers and metadata; freeze maximum frame length and IP MTU to fit complete frames before implementation. Physical RAM chip count remains unresolved.

Flow control: Grant unicast only when the destination advertises credit for a complete frame; reserve that credit until completion. Broadcast requires credit from all intended admitted receivers. Timeouts revoke stale credits; bounded queues and retry/error reporting prevent indefinite blocking. Use flow control first for receiver pressure, not automatic rate changes.

Host service: No per-byte interrupt requirement. Aurelia at 250 kbit/s has 128 CPU clocks per raw byte at 4 MHz; Aurelia+ at 500 kbit/s has 96 at 6 MHz. Validate worst-case service latency. A persistently slow host may advertise a lower configured ceiling.

before.name: Logix Video Card for Apple II
before.description: Logix-developed open-ecosystem expansion, independent of DRI’s development obligations.

specification.host_interface: Apple II slot decode and driver ROM; preserve native memory map and avoid other cards.
specification.software: Native Apple II 6502 drivers, callable libraries and examples; applications must use the card API. No CP/M port, Z80 CPU or transparent redirection of existing graphics.
specification.host_access: Windowed/addressed access to onboard video RAM; onboard display refresh continues independently. No extra general-purpose host RAM is implied.
specification.display_modes: Reuse Aurelia controller text/bitmap capabilities subject to card/monitor qualification. 80-column output requires a compatible 640-pixel monitor. Host CPU determines drawing throughput.
specification.sprite_policy: All five sprites in every supported Aurelia-family mode using exclusive 1 KiB SRAM; host-specific upload interface. No Aurelia system DMA controller on this card.

composition_definition.element_type: Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM on separate bus

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

requirements.description: Dedicated slot; powered-off replacement only; host interface, power rails and signal integrity require qualification.
Qualification pending.

before.description: Logix Artemis 64 KiB video controller card

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: With palette-list mode enabled reserve 0xFA00–0xFFFF (1536 bytes); framebuffer/text/font allocations use 0x0000–0xF9FF. Text/font and bitmap layouts remain exclusive. Five sprites retain separate 1 KiB SRAM.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: Two 16K x 16-bit banks; ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Preserve independent refresh and bounded host access.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

technical_definition.athena_qualification: Existing card baseline selected; Athena host electrical/firmware compatibility remains a release gate.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

requirements.description: New controller, 64 KiB DRAM decoding, palette sequencer and host/DMA arbitration require timing, power and release qualification.

Arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.

Monitor policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

Feature continuity ID is defined by {feature_continuity_id}.

Policy ID is defined by {memory_layout_policy_id}.

Mode exclusivity: With palette-list mode enabled reserve 0xFA00–0xFFFF (1536 bytes); framebuffer/text/font allocations use 0x0000–0xF9FF. Text/font and bitmap layouts remain exclusive. Five sprites retain separate 1 KiB SRAM.

Font policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.

Page flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

Policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.

Physical organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

composition_history.description: Professional hardware specification and composition from the Autodesk handover

specification.slot: One general 32-bit expansion slot; coexists with the dedicated primary video card
specification.mode_policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

palette_list.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.
palette_list.execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.
palette_list.long_gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.
palette_list.frame_state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.
palette_list.write_limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.
palette_list.cad_policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

acceleration: Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping
Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations
Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600
specification.redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.
specification.sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.
specification.monitor_modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.
specification.host_integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.

composition_definition.element_type: Separate 1 KiB sprite SRAM; not charged against 128 KiB display RAM

The separate sprite sram is {separate_sprite_sram_bytes} bytes.

Mode policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

Legacy card ID is defined by {legacy_card_id}.

Acceleration:

Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping.

Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations.

All-octant integer line drawing.

Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600.

Redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.

Sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.

Monitor modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.

Host integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.

Base address: {palette_list_base_address}.

End address: {palette_list_end_address}.

The reserved is {palette_list_reserved_bytes} bytes.

Maximum commands: {palette_list_maximum_commands}.

The command is {palette_list_command_bytes} bytes.

Encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.

Register count: {palette_list_register_count}.

Execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.

Long gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.

Frame state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.

Write limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.

Cad policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

specification.scan: 800x600 progressive; 60 Hz production target subject to OEM qualification
specification.oem_basis: Period 17-inch monochrome OEM assembly, with Ball HD17H family as a candidate rather than a confirmed supplier. Published Ball HD 26-36 kHz range does not meet the 37.5 kHz target without modification. Its digital video amplifier is not evidence of grayscale support.
specification.qualification: Ball documents 26-36 kHz horizontal and 40-80 Hz vertical; optional linear amplifier is 35 MHz typical. 60 Hz at the selected totals needs a qualified OEM deflection revision. Pixel clock is not analog bandwidth: test actual contrast, grayscale settling, geometry and corner focus. 56 Hz/35 kHz is a fallback engineering option, not a silently substituted retail specification.
specification.oem: Ball HD-series HD17H, 17-inch horizontal-format OEM assembly, analog/linear-video option
specification.signal_path: Logix digital pixel index -> AION palette/controller -> 4-bit intensity DAC -> level-matched Ball analog input and linear amplifier. TTL/ECL-only input is not sufficient.
specification.rgb_palette_mapping: Preserve the 12-bit RGB command format. For grayscale, equal-channel values 000,111,...,FFF map to the corresponding 16 intensity codes. Other RGB values use a documented fixed luminance mapping, with DAC/gamma calibration qualified on the actual CRT.

normal_view.description: Lower RAM, including CP/M page zero and application memory

organization.note: This is the normal application mapping. Within it, 7000–EFFF remains switchable in 4 KB pages. A system call can temporarily map ROM or video RAM there, preserving and later restoring any hidden RAM. F000–FFFF remains common system RAM.
organization.dma_addressing: Physical bank selections are latched per transfer; CPU mapping changes cannot redirect DMA.
organization.refresh: AION system controller refreshes all installed system DRAM independently of CPU activity.

normal_view.description: Base and expansion RAM, including CP/M page zero and application memory. The card supplies B000–EFFF.
Stable runtime entry code, system stack and critical state.

expanded_organization.note: The card fills B000–EFFF with RAM in the normal view. ROM, cartridges and video RAM use temporary overlays within 7000–EFFF; the underlying RAM retains its contents.
expanded_organization.dma_addressing: Physical bank selections are latched per transfer; CPU mapping changes cannot redirect DMA.
expanded_organization.refresh: AION system controller refreshes all installed system DRAM independently of CPU activity.

physical_population.mapping_note: Existing mapper and common-system-RAM reservations remain unchanged; physical bank/page decode must implement the logical normal view.

software_compatibility.adaptive_text: Applications query usable columns/rows instead of selecting behavior from model name.
software_compatibility.native_40_column_mode: Native 40x25 and 80x25 text on both hosts; usable width depends on monitor capabilities.

exact FDD mechanism plus a controller/data separator (not currently a named base part)
motherboard ROM capacity/package/count and cartridge connectors

clock/reset/interrupt circuitry
complete mainboard, PSU, enclosure and harnesses. Specify motherboard versus controller-chip integration.

Populate one shared Aurelia video controller and eight AION-manufactured 4116-equivalent 16Kx1 DRAMs (16 KiB). Qualify CPU arbitration at the host clock, refresh, pixel FIFO deadlines, package, rails and external video/control line drivers.

Provide three independent point-to-point FlexiBUS host ports, including connectors, transceivers, protection and power budget; qualify simultaneous keyboard, disk and printer service. Controller die count depends on ports per die.

Qualify CPU bus handover at 4 and 6 MHz, bounded DMA bursts, device-ready waits, completion interrupts and abort/reset recovery.
Verify independent refresh for every installed physical bank, including hidden banks and Aurelia 16 KiB expansion; derive deadlines from qualified DRAM ordering codes.
Freeze package/pinout, external buffers, memory decode, bank-latched DMA addressing and simultaneous video/peripheral stress tests.

assembly_requirements.description: Confirm package/pinout, supply rails, retention, refresh deadlines and 6 MHz host timing.

Populate one shared Aurelia video controller and eight AION-manufactured 4116-equivalent 16Kx1 DRAMs (16 KiB). Qualify CPU arbitration at the host clock, refresh, pixel FIFO deadlines, package, rails and external video/control line drivers.
Qualify dual-drive controller/mechanisms, ROM images/capacities, 6 MHz host timing and PSU/thermal deltas.

Provide three independent point-to-point FlexiBUS host ports, including connectors, transceivers, protection and power budget; qualify simultaneous keyboard, disk and printer service. Controller die count depends on ports per die.
PCB dimensions, layer stack, finish, connectors, fitted passives and reference designators
Power per rail, startup/thermal limits and region-specific power configuration
Firmware image capacity/revision, programming and verification
Assembly routing, test fixtures, cycle times, yield/rework/scrap and packout
Qualify AION 1Kx4 static cells, 250 ns cycle target, retention while powered, +5 V supply and 18-pin DIP compatibility before launch.
Test two-chip 1Kx8 sprite bus, CPU/DMA write arbitration and worst-case five-sprite overlap.
Qualify CPU bus handover at 4 and 6 MHz, bounded DMA bursts, device-ready waits, completion interrupts and abort/reset recovery.
Verify independent refresh for every installed physical bank, including hidden banks and Aurelia 16 KiB expansion; derive deadlines from qualified DRAM ordering codes.
Freeze package/pinout, external buffers, memory decode, bank-latched DMA addressing and simultaneous video/peripheral stress tests.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

memory.population_policy: Two matched 32-bit modules per capacity bank, selected independently on the 32-bit bus. Fill banks in order; all ranks require decoding and refresh. Cross-host connector/timing qualification pending.
memory.capacity_policy: Installed configuration is specified; maximum board capacity/socket count remain open and are not the CPU address-space limit.

os_rom.execution: Directly executable shared read-only AIONix2 code; private writable data and patch overlays in DRAM.
os_rom.implementation: A replaceable AIONix 2 system cartridge is fitted to every computer; chip organisation, connector, access timing and exchange procedure require qualification.

video.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: With palette-list mode enabled reserve 0xFA00–0xFFFF (1536 bytes); framebuffer/text/font allocations use 0x0000–0xF9FF. Text/font and bitmap layouts remain exclusive. Five sprites retain separate 1 KiB SRAM.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: Two 16K x 16-bit banks; ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Preserve independent refresh and bounded host access.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

memory.population_policy: Two matched 32-bit modules per capacity bank, selected independently on the 32-bit bus. Fill banks in order; all ranks require decoding and refresh. Cross-host connector/timing qualification pending.

os_rom.execution: Directly executable shared read-only AIONix2 code; private writable data and patch overlays in DRAM.
os_rom.implementation: A replaceable AIONix 2 system cartridge is fitted to every computer; chip organisation, connector, access timing and exchange procedure require qualification.

video.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: With palette-list mode enabled reserve 0xFA00–0xFFFF (1536 bytes); framebuffer/text/font allocations use 0x0000–0xF9FF. Text/font and bitmap layouts remain exclusive. Five sprites retain separate 1 KiB SRAM.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: Two 16K x 16-bit banks; ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Preserve independent refresh and bounded host access.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

technical_profile.software_policy: Preserve documented ERA AIONix binaries through versioned compatibility; individual applications and editions require qualification. External application ROM cartridges are not added by the internal system ROM decision.

Character row cache bytes per bank: {video_character_row_cache_bytes_per_bank}.

The total is {video_character_row_cache_total_bytes} bytes.

Character row cache purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

The pixel clock is {video_timing_budget_pixel_clock_mhz} MHz.

Timing budget renderer pixels per step: {video_timing_budget_renderer_pixels_per_step}.

The renderer step is {video_timing_budget_renderer_step_mhz} MHz.

Timing budget page drain microseconds: {video_timing_budget_page_drain_microseconds}.

Timing budget qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

Arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.

Monitor policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

reporting.continuity: Extend Abacus 2.0 report/document layouts, spreadsheet fields and one-off/repeating sections.
reporting.presentation: Retain standard TUI editing/navigation; add capability-aware graphical preview with titles, axes and legends. Support monochrome patterns and available display modes through the display API.
reporting.output: Print reports and charts through supported printer drivers; define pagination and refresh stale query/formula results before output.

data_interchange.bpi_continuity: Retain versioned BPI summary imports as independent planning inputs with reconciliation and decimal validation; no ledger write-back or live database connection.
data_interchange.csv: Schema-mapped CSV import with quoted fields, delimiter/character encoding selection, explicit date and decimal conventions, null handling, text preservation for identifiers and rejected-record diagnostics. data_interchange.vsam: Import host-exported sequential logical records from supported VSAM datasets using a supplied field/record layout. data_interchange.vsam_conversion: Declare supported record boundaries, lengths, offsets, keys and character encoding; convert EBCDIC, supported binary, packed-decimal and zoned-decimal fields explicitly. Reject unsupported layouts without silently changing values.
data_interchange.migration: Versioned document format; preserve supported older worksheets and reports. Older Abacus/Pulse editions must reject unsupported new features before writing. Explicit value-only export is a lossy interchange option.

Broader query capabilities and competitive response to Lotus 1-2-3 in a later Abacus version.
release_scope.resource_policy: Qualify real Artemis 128/256 KiB configurations and later Artemis PRO separately. Record application/OS memory, storage, dataset size and timings; larger jobs may require expansion or disk-backed execution. No new minimum RAM or maximum row count is asserted.
release_scope.acceptance_workflow: Import sales records, join customer/product information, calculate margins, group by region, print a graphical report, save/reopen, then repeat using a Pulse script.
acceptance_requirements: Measure memory, disk I/O, import/query/recalculation/report times and compression on named datasets.
Verify import conversion/rejections, decimal rounding, nulls, duplicate lookup keys and join cardinality.
Verify cancellation, grouped undo, edit visibility, dependency invalidation, save recovery and unsupported-version rejection.

internal_organization.description: Operate video, keyboard, floppy and FlexiBUS hardware; discover devices and register compatible drivers.

internal_organization.description: Translate CP/M console, printer and disk operations into Logix driver calls.

internal_organization.name: CP/M 1.4-derived BDOS
internal_organization.residence: System cartridge; mutable state in RAM
internal_organization.description: Preserve file/application services; adapt disk-format assumptions and code for banked ROM execution.

internal_organization.name: CP/M 1.4-derived CCP
internal_organization.residence: System cartridge; command buffers in RAM
internal_organization.description: Interpret commands, launch disk/cartridge applications and use shared command-line editing.

internal_organization.name: Logix TUI and shared services
internal_organization.residence: CP/M system cartridge; mutable state in reserved RAM; hardware operations delegated to drivers
internal_organization.description: Own the shared application-facing screen and keyboard API, editing controls, menus, forms, lists, popup windows, clipboard service and workspace entry/return support. Business Tools and other compatible applications call these services rather than carrying a second shared TUI library.

internal_organization.name: Utilities and applications
internal_organization.description: Use standard CP/M calls and, when Logix-aware, the versioned extension interface.

logix_requirements: Preserve standard CP/M entry points, loading conventions and available-memory boundaries.
Adapt both BIOS and relevant BDOS assumptions to Aurelia floppy formats.
Keep bank-switching entry code, stack and critical interrupt handling permanently accessible.
Separate ROM code/constants from RAM state; adapt self-modifying routines.
Discover cartridge/device ROMs through defined, versioned interfaces.
Map Logix peripherals to standard CP/M console, printer and disk services.
Provide a separate versioned Logix service interface and C bindings.
Drivers use bounded DMA transfers with physical-bank descriptors and device-ready handshakes; abort/drain transfers before warm boot or reusing buffers.
Video API exposes dedicated sprite SRAM, atomic descriptor swaps and upload-port backpressure; use programmed I/O fallback where peripherals lack DMA endpoints.

tui_features.name: Layout and screen
tui_features.description: Query usable dimensions, clip and scroll; separate document coordinates from screen coordinates.

tui_features.name: Adaptive layouts
tui_features.description: Compact 40-column and expanded 80-column layouts; dialogs, long names and errors fit either width.

tui_features.name: Semantic colors
tui_features.description: Normal text, selection and warning roles map to color or monochrome attributes.

tui_features.name: Input
tui_features.description: Structured character, function/navigation key and modifier events; blocking input and polling.

tui_features.name: Controls
tui_features.description: Fields, lists, menus, dialogs, popup windows and consistent focus movement.

tui_features.name: Editing
tui_features.description: Common selection, insertion/deletion and clipboard commands.

tui_features.name: Clipboard
tui_features.description: Explicit formats, lengths, bounded capacity, ownership and errors.

tui_features.name: Context lifecycle
tui_features.description: Create/destroy and activate/deactivate contexts; redraw when needed. A context describes an assigned display region, which may be the full Aurelia screen.

tui_features.name: Timing
tui_features.description: System timing and keyboard-repeat services replace CPU-speed-dependent loops.

compatibility_notes: Ordinary CP/M applications keep character/file services; rich TUI behavior requires use of Logix APIs.
Shared TUI routines do not require multitasking; applications may remain sequential.
Clipboard capacity, exact widgets and workspace behavior remain implementation decisions.
Keep the same API behavior across Aurelia, Aurelia+ and Artemis.
Do not assume display stride, video RAM address, last column or direct peripheral registers.
Legacy CP/M console behavior is preserved; Logix-aware interfaces use the documented editing conventions.
Artemis implementation mediates process access to shared clipboard and display services.

tui_ownership.boundary: System services supply reusable controls and clipboard/workspace mechanisms. Applications own their documents, calculations, file-management workflows and calendar records.

portable_runtime.ownership: System owns shared TUI implementation; Business Tools applications consume it.
portable_runtime.capability_discovery: Report supported services, limits and usable display configurations.
portable_runtime.abi_policy: Stable binary interfaces within this target; shared C API across targets.

implementation_design.title: BPI transactional client/server v1
implementation_design.architecture: Thin Z80/ERA clients send bounded business operations to an Artemis PRO server. Query evaluation, indexes, validation, accounting posting and transactions execute on the server; clients do not fetch arbitrary database pages.

transactions.concurrency: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.
transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

protocol.transport: Length-framed requests over TCP; bounded messages and chunked results.
protocol.duplicate_suppression: Store committed write request IDs and outcomes durably. After reconnect, clients query status or retry with the same ID; never post the same payment twice.

data_integrity: Amounts use explicitly scaled integers/decimal rules, never unspecified binary floating-point rounding.
Record currency, rounding, posting dates, account periods and unique document IDs.
Cross-module posting is atomic and produces an append-only audit record.
operations: Backup captures a consistent checkpoint plus required logs; test restoration onto a clean disk.
Bounded log growth, disk-full handling and operator-visible recovery status
Plan backups and report traffic around the negotiated shared 100/250/500/1000 kbit/s raw LAN budget and measured payload throughput; slower admitted hosts limit the whole network.

initial_limits.client_policy: Bounded pages of results and forms; no entire-table download or whole-document duplication.

acceptance_tests: Full disk, corrupt log tail and failed backup restore

distribution.network_operation: Start under the existing networking OS, connect to server, and load further modules/data over the network; bootstrap remains local.
distribution.data_access: Business transactions, validation and database writes remain server-side; clients do not directly modify shared database files.

compatibility_policy.eligibility: Any manufacturer or independent integrator may implement the published environment without a bespoke partnership or mandatory certification.
compatibility_policy.binary: Existing Z80 binaries require compatible instruction execution and the specified OS/runtime and memory behaviour; CP/M alone is insufficient. Other processors need an appropriate port or execution solution.
compatibility_policy.hardware: Native video, keyboards, disks and printers may be exposed through adapters. FlexiBUS and Logix video hardware are separate optional profiles. Full hardware clones may implement those published interfaces under their applicable terms.
compatibility_policy.applications: Named supported platforms are tested configurations, not an exclusive permission list. Independently implemented environments may run properly licensed applications; certification identifies precisely what AION tested.
compatibility_policy.delivery: Printed manuals/source listings and disks; host/media conversion quoted separately.
compatibility_policy.certification: Optional, configuration- and version-specific. Manufacturer-declared compatibility is distinct from AION-tested application compatibility. FlexiBUS electrical/protocol and Logix display tests are separate claims.

implementation_design.arbitration: Independent display-DRAM and sprite-SRAM buses. Display reads and full-array refresh have bounded host/DMA backpressure. Sprite fetches use the separate SRAM bus and existing staging/shifters; completed FIFO banks preserve raster order.
implementation_design.text_fetch: Cache 80 character codes and 80 attributes; prefetch the next row into the second 160-byte cache over eight glyph scanlines. Expand each glyph byte to eight 4-bit pixels; prefetch sprite rows and apply fixed priority before publishing pixels.
implementation_design.line_repeat: Re-fetch repeated bitmap lines; FIFO capacity is not an additional framebuffer or guaranteed retained scanline. Validate 320x100x4 bandwidth and refresh at the selected DRAM grade.

clock_targets.scope: 14.31818 MHz short scanout/counter path; renderer uses block expansion and clock enables, not a full CPU at pixel rate. Process-corner qualification required.

manufacturing_planning.process: 3–3.5 micron NMOS; laser-written process-matched masks from secret facility; wafer fabrication at AION Labs.
external_functions: Two AION 2114-equivalent SRAM chips on a separate sprite bus; enlarged interface package/PCB allowance costed at assembly level

engines.renderer: Dedicated fetch/address, eight-pixel glyph expansion, colour selection and fixed-priority sprite compositor; not a general-purpose CPU. Runs when a free FIFO bank and source data are available.
engines.scanout: Independent fixed-raster sequencer reads completed 4-bit pixels and generates sync. Both engines use the same master clock with clock enables.
engines.fifo: Four 40-byte addressed banks with output latches; ordered circular FREE/FILLING/READY/READING ownership. Publish complete banks only; backpressure on full FIFO; prefill before active display.
engines.underrun: Continue sync, emit border colour and latch diagnostic status; never read a partially rendered bank.

timing_budget.qualification: 100 display-DRAM reads average 37.5 us; 40 sprite bytes take 10 us on a separate bus. Descriptor reads and row transitions also need scheduling. Prove local FIFO deadlines, refresh, repeated bitmap lines and uploads; these averages are not a timing proof.

implementation_design.sprite_access: Two AION 2114-equivalent chips form an exclusive 1 KiB 8-bit SRAM bank. Auto-increment upload ports arbitrate CPU/DMA writes against sprite reads; descriptor-bank selection latches at vertical blank.

pixel_buffer.location: Inside reused Aurelia controller
pixel_buffer.policy: FREE/FILLING/READY/READING banks; output latches and serializer. Never overwrite active bank; underrun preserves sync.

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

sprites.coordinate_space: Logical mode pixels; scale together with the background. Signed 16-bit X and Y; clip at screen edges.
sprites.priority: Lower sprite number wins; all sprites overlay background/text.
sprites.registers: Two descriptor banks hold signed 16-bit X/Y, enable and reserved controls. CPU/DMA uses auto-incrementing SRAM upload ports.
sprites.allocation_policy: Five sprites in every text/bitmap mode, including double-buffered backgrounds. Sprite SRAM never consumes display DRAM.
sprites.descriptor_allocation_note: 80 bytes of live two-bank descriptors within a 128-byte reserved area; 48 bytes padding. 640 pattern + 128 descriptor + 256 scratch bytes = 1024.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

requirements.description: External 16×4116 DRAM and 2×2114 sprite SRAM; integrated 640-byte pixel FIFO and 320-byte row cache. Die-area estimate 80 mm² (60–110), about 65,000–95,000 transistors including SRAM; not a released layout. Qualify timing, large-package pin count, analog-free digital logic and one respin.
